deviations.derivation: The required test name coaxial_cylinders_emit_circle_and_equal_radius_refuses_overlap includes 'emit_circle', but the arm-5 cylinder~cylinder admitted subset never emits a circle: equal-radius coaxial cylinders refuse UnsupportedPairClass and different-radius coaxial cylinders are exactly Disjoint (the packet's own arm-5 spec). The 'emit circle' is read as the arm-2 perpendicular plane~cylinder cut -- a circle coaxial with the cylinder (center on the cylinder's axis, radius the cylinder's exact radius, axis the plane's raw normal) -- which the test asserts first, then asserts the two coaxial-cylinder behaviors on the NAMED variants exactly. No arm behavior deviates from the packet's per-arm specification.

The two required public signatures trip clippy::large_enum_variant (denied by the crate's #![deny(clippy::all)]): CertifiedPairParticipant carries CertifiedEmbeddedCylinder unboxed (the D-routing signature, ~456 bytes vs the small plane/sphere witnesses) and CertifiedPairResult carries CertifiedPairContact by value (the D-result signature). Boxing would change the required public surface, so the lint is suppressed with a justification at the ITEM level (#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)] on the two enums), which H-1's letter permits ('NO module-level allow' -- item-level allows are the crate's own precedent, e.g. #[allow(dead_code)] on CylinderValidityCertificate::discharged). The suppressed lint is the only clippy finding the new files would otherwise contribute.

The value leaves of the Circle arms are enclosure-valued through CertifiedInterval::sqrt / div (arm 3 plane~sphere radius, arm 4 sphere~sphere radical radius). If a directed-rounded enclosure cannot be constructed (div by a zero-containing denominator or sqrt of a negative interval image -- impossible for the packet's exact screens on ordinary fixtures but not excluded in pathological cancellation), the arm refuses UnsupportedPairClass rather than emitting a guessed or unwrapped value. This is a value-construction refusal, not an admission-screen tolerance: the DECISIONS remain exact expansion sign tests.

The coincidence screens (coaxial equal-radius cylinders, coincident spheres) compare the two PositiveFinite radii by exact f64 equality, and the internal-tangency Point branch selects its construction formula by the exact sign of Expansion::from_sum(r1, -r2). Both are exact predicates over the witnesses' own representation f64 values (no computed quantity, no epsilon, no interval straddle at admission time), consistent with D-exact. Recorded because a reader might otherwise expect every screen to be a multi-term Expansion sum; the radii ARE the representation's declared values, so a direct exact comparison is the same predicate class.
